title: Do Generate–Verify–Repair Guards Improve LLM NetOps Outputs? A Paired Emulator Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (n=200 natural-language NetOps intents; study_id cnd-001-5f3a) comparing ungated LLM generation to a bounded generate–verify–repair (GVR) pipeline applied to the same initial LLM candidate. Generation used gpt-5-mini and the guarded arm applied a deterministic three-stage validator and a deterministic rule-based repair operator (repair_budget ≤1; no extra LLM calls). Artifact-backed primary outcomes: baseline successes 199/200 (0.995), guarded 200/200 (1.000); paired contingency n11=199, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.015]. The preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target is excluded by the observed CI because the realized baseline was near-ceiling. Execution accounting: model_calls_used = 201; deterministic repair invocations = 1. All prompts, provider traces, validator traces, repair trace, and analysis artifacts are archived in the study evidence bundle.

sections.introduction: Automating routine NetOps changes with large language models (LLMs) promises reduced manual effort but raises a core operational-safety question: do LLM-produced configuration artifacts execute correctly when applied to control planes? Prior work documents structured-output failures (missing commands, misordering, protected-field modification) and proposes mitigations such as retrieval-augmentation, constrained decoding, verifier-assisted repair, and multi-stage tool augmentation. Despite these proposals, rigorous execution-grounded evidence quantifying the marginal benefit of applying a bounded deterministic repair to the same initial LLM candidate under tight hosted-call budgets is scarce. We preregistered and executed a paired experiment (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) that isolates the “repair-on-same-candidate” estimand: a shared initial candidate is used for both baseline (ungated acceptance) and guarded (validator ± deterministic repair) arms. Our contributions are (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired evaluation under the shared-candidate estimand; (2) concise algorithmic descriptions of the deterministic three-stage validator and the deterministic, rule-based repair operator used in the guarded pipeline; and (3) complete execution accounting and exact-test justification appropriate for small-discordant-pair inference.
sections.related_work: LLMs for NetOps have been studied as intent-to-configuration synthesizers, with surveys and prototypes showing capabilities and recurrent structured-output failures. Mitigation approaches span constrained/grammar-aware decoding, retrieval-augmentation and RAG, schema grounding, and verifier-assisted repair; cross-domain evidence (e.g., NL2SQL, clinical RAG) indicates deterministic validators combined with grounding reduce hallucinations but require domain adaptation. Deterministic/formal verification tools (NetKAT variants, ensemble verifiers) and emulator-backed validation are natural assurance layers but have known limitations around dynamic control-plane behaviors. Generate–verify–repair (GVR) architectures are advocated in the literature, yet fully instrumented, reproducible, execution-grounded paired evaluations that isolate low-call-budget designs remain rare. Our study addresses this empirical gap by measuring the auditable, low-call-cost yield of a deterministic repair operator applied to the same initial candidate.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and design: The preregistered confirmatory protocol (study_id cnd-001-5f3a) specified a paired, shared-initial-generation design with n=200 curated natural-language intents. For each intent the hosted model produced one initial candidate (shared candidate). That candidate was scored directly as the baseline arm and also passed to the guarded arm. The guarded arm ran a deterministic validator (three stages) and, if the validator reported a repairable violation family (per a preregistered repairable set), invoked a deterministic, rule-based repair operator limited to a single deterministic transformation (repair_budget ≤1). No additional LLM calls were permitted for repair in the confirmatory run. The primary estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline). The preregistered primary hypothesis test is the exact two-sided McNemar (implemented as the exact binomial on discordant pairs). Planned maximum hosted-model calls = 400; realized model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; deterministic repair-stage calls = 1). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the canonical validator.
sections.results:
Execution and primary outcomes: The confirmatory run completed all planned episodes (400 episodes = 200 paired intents) with no provider/API failures. Condition-level artifact-backed counts (analysis/condition_summary.csv) show baseline_successes = 199/200 (0.995) and guarded_successes = 200/200 (1.000). The paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) is n11 = 199, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0; paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.005.

Power assumption and small-discordant inference: The preregistered power analysis assumed a baseline ≈0.5 and targeted a 15 percentage-point absolute effect at n = 200. The observed baseline (0.995) is near-ceiling and substantially compresses the number of discordant pairs that can appear under the paired estimand. Empirically, the observed discordant-pair counts were n = n10 + n01 = 1 (n10 = 1, n01 = 0). Under these small-discordant counts the exact two-sided McNemar (exact-binomial on discordant pairs) yields p = 1.0 for the observed ordering; the paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729) for the guarded − baseline difference is [0.0, 0.015] (analysis artifacts archived). Because the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target lies well outside the observed CI, the confirmatory data do not support that magnitude of improvement under the shared-candidate estimand. This is a formal post-hoc limitation: the near-ceiling baseline reduces statistical sensitivity for the originally targeted large absolute effect.

Repair accounting and exemplar summary: The deterministic validator reported validation_before.valid == false in exactly one confirmatory episode; deterministic repair invocations = 1, and that single deterministic repair converted the episode into a validator-passing final configuration (thereby producing the sole guarded-only success, n10 = 1). Provider-call accounting records hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 201, cache_miss_count = 201, and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1}. The single repair's complete validator and repair traces are archived in the evidence bundle for audit. For compact illustration, six representative exemplars (published with the archived manifest) include difficulty labels: among those six exemplars the labels are 1 medium, 2 hard, and 3 very_hard; the full per-task difficulty labels for all 200 confirmatory intents are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a). Readers and auditors can inspect the manifest to obtain the complete per-task label distribution and the artifact path for the single repaired episode. Analysis artifacts (paired_contingency_table.csv, condition_summary.csv, and the bootstrap parameters) contain the exact numbers reported above (see analysis/* files in the evidence bundle).
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: Under the shared-initial-generation estimand the ungated gpt-5-mini generator produced near-perfect candidates in this curated bank (199/200). Deterministic validators provide structured violation codes that enable targeted deterministic repairs; in a low-error regime the marginal yield of a conservative, deterministic repair applied to the same candidate is small but auditable and low-cost. For operators constrained by model-call budgets, the shared-candidate guarded design preserves low hosted-call cost while providing an assurance gate. If operators prioritize maximal success-rate and can afford additional calls, independent-resampling (multiple independent generations per intent) or LLM-guided iterative repair can increase success at higher provider cost and governance complexity.

Threats to validity and practical caveats: Internal validity for the paired estimand is strong due to deterministic scoring and complete episode accounting. Construct validity depends on emulator fidelity: our deterministic emulator models control-plane state deterministically but cannot capture dynamic runtime effects such as BGP convergence timing or device firmware idiosyncrasies. External validity is limited by a single LLM (gpt-5-mini) and a synthetic, curated bank focused on small single- and small multi-device changes; extrapolation to multivendor CLI diversity or adversarially crafted intents is constrained. Conclusion validity is limited by the near-ceiling baseline that produced only one discordant pair; the exact McNemar is the correct small-sample test but offers limited sensitivity when discordants are rare. These limitations mean the observed negligible marginal improvement applies to this estimand and task distribution, not to broader NetOps workloads or alternative estimands.
sections.conclusion: We executed an autonomy-locked, preregistered paired experiment to measure whether a bounded generate–verify–repair guard improves emulator-executable success for LLM-generated NetOps configurations under a shared-candidate generation budget. Ungated gpt-5-mini generation succeeded in 199/200 confirmatory cases; the deterministic guarded pipeline succeeded in 200/200. The observed paired difference = 0.005 (exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; paired-bootstrap 95% CI [0.0, 0.015]) does not support the preregistered 0.15 absolute-effect target because the baseline was near-ceiling; deterministic repair-on-same-candidate yielded a single low-cost, auditable correction in this confirmatory bank. Deterministic validators remain valuable auditable assurance gates; broader task banks, multivendor evaluations, and alternative estimands (e.g., independent-resampling) are needed to evaluate higher-yield repair strategies. All artifacts, validator/repair traces, and analysis code are archived for independent audit and re-analysis (see evidence bundle references below).

disclosure_statement:
This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock defined by the initial master prompt archived at provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human involvement prior to the lock was limited to selecting the topic family (Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps) and approving the master prompt. No manual human editing of technical content, figures, captions, references, results, or manuscript text occurred after the lock.

Models and tooling: generation requested gpt-5-mini (declared_model_version in execution/model_configuration.json). Validation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementing syntactic parsing, structural/workflow checks, and deterministic emulator application. Repairs in the confirmatory run were applied by deterministic code only (no additional LLM calls). The execution environment used Dockerized Mininet+FRR images orchestrated by adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1.

Preregistered and enforced settings (not altered post-lock) include: primary estimand = paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline; confirmatory sample = n=200 paired intents; maximum model-call budget = 400; repair budget ≤1 deterministic repair iteration; primary analysis = exact McNemar two-sided (exact-binomial on discordant pairs); bootstrap CIs = 10,000 resamples, seed = 1729. Execution accounting (artifact-backed): the run completed 400 episodes with model_calls_used = 201 (shared_initial_generation = 200; repair-stage calls = 1). All prompts, provider-call traces, responses, validator traces, repair traces (the single invoked repair trace), analysis artifacts, and the execution manifest are archived in the study evidence bundle (see execution/execution_manifest.json and execution/task_manifest.jsonl; task_manifest SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a).
limitations: Synthetic, curated confirmatory task bank focused on small single- and small multi-device changes; not comprehensive of production NetOps workloads (multivendor CLI dialects, hardware idiosyncrasies, dynamic control-plane timing).
Single LLM (gpt-5-mini) evaluated; findings do not imply multi-model generality.
Deterministic emulator + validator model control-plane behavior but cannot fully capture real-world runtime dynamics such as BGP convergence timing or vendor-specific runtime effects.
Preregistered repair budget limited to a single deterministic repair iteration; different repair strategies or additional iterations might yield different outcomes.
Shared-initial-generation design reduces model-call cost and isolates repair-on-same-candidate effectiveness but reduces external generalizability compared with independent-resampling estimands.
Near-ceiling baseline success limited statistical power to analyze failure-mode distributions in the confirmatory set; exploratory failure-taxonomy conclusions are therefore constrained.
Adversarial or out-of-distribution intents (e.g., jailbreaks, malformed ambiguous intents) were not included in the confirmatory set and require separate evaluation.

Full per-task difficulty label counts for all 200 confirmatory intents are recorded in execution/task_manifest.jsonl in the archived evidence bundle (SHA-256: eb2f045f8a6214eb6d814e16f5d95e0120bd89973951b6fe14084bda4e3efb4a); the manuscript references that manifest rather than enumerating the full 200-line distribution inline to preserve concise presentation while preserving auditable reproducibility.
